claims.text: The target material is a powder-metallurgy and HIP-consolidated W–Cu composite containing either discrete W particles or interconnected W ligaments in a Cu matrix.
The proposed single intervention is rapid thermal annealing immediately after consolidation.
The rapid thermal anneal should be conducted at approximately 900 °C for 5–10 minutes in argon with controlled heating and cooling ramps.
Rapid thermal annealing at the proposed conditions induces localized interdiffusion at W/Cu interfaces.
Controlled interdiffusion forms a compositionally graded W/Cu interfacial region.
The graded interfacial region reduces the interfacial-energy disparity between W and Cu.
Reduced interfacial-energy disparity suppresses phase separation and interfacial void nucleation.
Compositional gradients at untreated W/Cu interfaces promote de-mixing under thermal cycling and irradiation.
Interfacial interdiffusion strengthens bonding between W and Cu.
Stronger bonding and reduced void formation create more continuous thermal-transport pathways.
The RTA-treated composite will retain lower interfacial void density and less phase separation than the untreated composite during high-heat-flux and irradiation exposure.
The RTA-treated composite will exhibit higher effective thermal conductivity than the untreated composite after service-like thermal and irradiation exposure.
Untreated W–Cu composites typically undergo phase separation and interfacial void formation during repeated thermal cycling and irradiation.
Phase separation and interfacial void formation degrade the thermal conductivity of untreated W–Cu composites.
The proposed treatment is limited to W–Cu composites that can tolerate brief exposure to 900 °C without excessive grain coarsening.
The proposed service domain is high thermal loading with moderate irradiation, representative of joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components.
